Case: A technology-diffusion strategy predicts supplier growth from public patent text. The database dates each record by application submission even when the text was not published until much later, and trades are assigned to the submission month. Case: An early-stage patent model ranks semantic novelty but does not specify whether novelty predicts profitable innovation, speculative overvaluation, or costly experimentation. Its explanation charts identify unusual words without distinguishing these mechanisms. The reviewer is choosing the first substantive research action.
rationale: The novelty measure needs an economically directional, falsifiable claim rather than an interpretation based only on unusual language.

Case: A macro-surprise strategy compares a survey median saved before release with the latest official historical series. Orders are delayed five minutes and priced from archived quotes, but later benchmark revisions alter the actual-minus-forecast surprise for many events. Case: A preregistered macro rule uses first-release data and passes independent event holdouts with acceptable gap exposure. It earns 5 basis points gross per round trip, but assumes the ordinary-session 1-basis-point round-trip spread. Archived quotes at its actual order times imply 7 basis points before fees, and the paper has not rerun fills using those release-window quotes. The signal timestamps themselves are correct.
rationale: The relevant 7-basis-point release-window spread exceeds the 5-basis-point gross edge and must be reflected in net results.
